title: sharp 0.32.6 processing untrusted uploads: bundled libvips/libheif/librsvg memory-corruption (CVE-2026-33327 et al.)
description: The image-processing library sharp is pinned to 0.32.6, which bundles libvips, libheif and librsvg builds affected by multiple published memory-corruption advisories (GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj, GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c, GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w). This application processes attacker-supplied images with this exact version on its upload endpoints.
impact: An authenticated user (any account — registration is open) uploading a crafted image (avatar/photo/exam scan) can trigger memory corruption in the image-decode pipeline. Demonstrated consequence class: process crash (event-loop death → API-wide DoS). Upper bound per advisories: potential RCE on glibc Linux, which would expose the PostgreSQL database holding LGPD-sensitive health data (CPF, exams, mental-health screenings).
remediation_steps: Upgrade sharp to >= 0.35.5 (fixes GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w / CVE-2026-96889, which also covers the libvips CVE-2026-33327/33328 and libheif fixes shipped in 0.35.0/0.35.4). Additionally remove `failOn: 'none'` so malformed images are rejected early, and run image decoding in a disposable worker/queue so a crash cannot take the API process down.
evidence:
**Advisory evidence:** `CVE-2026-33327` applies to `sharp` at installed version `0.32.6`. The advisory is fixed in `0.35.5`.

**Transitive dependency:** introduced by the direct dependency `sharp@0.32.6`.

**Dependency chain:** `sharp@0.32.6`

**Usage analysis:** the advisory's affected API is used in application code. Source-to-sink trace: POST /api/patients/:id/photo (src/routes/patient.routes.ts:321, multer upload.single) → savePatientPhoto (src/utils/storage.ts:108) → optimizeAvatar (src/utils/imageStorage.ts:11) → sharp(buffer, { failOn: 'none' }).resize().jpeg().toBuffer(). Same sink reached by POST /api/doctor/me/photo (src/routes/doctor.routes.ts:444 → src/utils/storage.ts:143), by POST /api/exams file upload (src/routes/exam.routes.ts:151 → saveExamFile → src/utils/storage.ts:159), and by POST /api/medications/scan-photo (aiLimiter-gated but open to any authenticated user). 'failOn: none' at imageStorage.ts:11 explicitly instructs sharp to keep processing malformed images, i.e. the hardened bail-out is disabled on every attacker-reachable path. No image source is trusted-only. This is a prioritization signal from static analysis, not a proof of exploitability or of safety.
assumptions: Advisory data verified against the trivy-offline GHSA database (web search unavailable in this sandbox); installed version 0.32.6 confirmed from node_modules. Exploitability assumes attacker can upload an image through any authenticated upload endpoint (patient photo, doctor photo, exam file, medication photo scan).

Same sink reached by POST /api/doctor/me/photo (src/routes/doctor.routes.ts:444 → src/utils/storage.ts:143), by POST /api/exams file upload (src/routes/exam.routes.ts:151 → saveExamFile → src/utils/storage.ts:159), and by POST /api/medications/scan-photo (aiLimiter-gated but open to any authenticated user). title: nodemailer 9.1.1 quadratic addressparser DoS via attacker-controlled recipients (CVE-2026-90776)
description: nodemailer is pinned to 9.1.1, which is inside the affected range of a quadratic-complexity address-parsing DoS (CVE-2026-90776 / GHSA-v53p-9fqp-m79j). This application feeds attacker-influenced email addresses into nodemailer on several flows.
impact: An unauthenticated attacker (lead form, signup) or low-privilege user (reminder/verification mails to their own registered address) can submit a crafted address string that blocks the Node.js event loop for several seconds per request; repeated submissions starve the single-process API and degrade all endpoints for all tenants of this health-data service.
remediation_steps: Upgrade nodemailer to >= 10.0.6 (fixes both CVE-2026-90776 and GHSA-v53p-9fqp-m79j). As defense in depth, validate/normalize recipient addresses with a strict RFC 5322 subset before passing them to nodemailer, and cap local-part length.
evidence:
**Advisory evidence:** `CVE-2026-90776` applies to `nodemailer` at installed version `9.1.1`. The advisory is fixed in `10.0.6`.

**Dependency chain:** `nodemailer@9.1.1`

**Usage analysis:** a call path from application code to the vulnerable function was proven. Source-to-sink trace: POST /api/public/lead (src/routes/lead.routes.ts:47, client-supplied `email` validated only by a basic regex) and POST /api/auth/register (attacker's own email) → sendWelcome/sendEmail (src/utils/mailer.ts) → nodemailer transport.sendMail({ to: email }) → addressparser quadratic path. Authenticated vector: src/jobs/reminderEmails.ts:71 sends to owner.email; password-reset and verification flows likewise use the registered address, which the user controls. The addressparser sink is exercised on every sendMail call, so the vulnerable code path is imported and executed routinely. This is a prioritization signal from static analysis, not a proof of exploitability or of safety.
assumptions: Advisory data verified against the trivy-offline GHSA database (web search unavailable in this sandbox); installed version 9.1.1 confirmed from node_modules. Exploitability assumes the attacker can control a recipient address that the app feeds to nodemailer — satisfied by signup email, password-reset recipient, and account deletion.

Authenticated vector: src/jobs/reminderEmails.ts:71 sends to owner.email; password-reset and verification flows likewise use the registered address, which the user controls. The addressparser sink is exercised on every sendMail call, so the vulnerable code path is imported and executed routinely.
dependency_metadata.contextual_cvss_reasoning: nodemailer 9.1.1 is imported at src/utils/mailer.ts:1 and sendEmail() passes the attacker-controlled `to` string into nodemailer's address parsing on every outbound mail. The attacker-controlled entry points are unauthenticated or free-signup flows: POST /api/auth/register (attacker chooses their own email), the password-reset flow (attacker requests reset to their own address), POST /api/public/lead (source-gated but email is client-supplied), and email-driven exam upload. A crafted local-part/domain containing RFC 5322 comment-separated atoms or a long whitespace-free run without '@' hits the quadratic path in addressparser, blocking the single Node.js event loop for seconds per request. Because the entire API shares one event loop, event-loop starvation degrades every endpoint, not just email (A:H). No confidentiality or integrity impact is demonstrated. privileges_required:N because registration and lead capture are open.

title: node-forge 1.4.0 (via firebase-admin) RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature-forgery vulnerability CVE-2026-85393
description: node-forge 1.4.0 is present via firebase-admin and fails to validate element count in nested DigestAlgorithm sequences during RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification (CVE-2026-85393, incomplete fix of CVE-2026-33894). Garbage bytes can be embedded to forge signatures for arbitrary messages under low-exponent RSA keys.
impact: If any reachable code path passed attacker-controlled signed material into node-forge's RSA verification, signatures could be forged. No such path was identified in this codebase; the finding documents the vulnerable dependency for upgrade tracking.
remediation_steps: Track the upstream node-forge fix (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-33894; no fixed release at scan time) and upgrade once published, or override the transitive resolution to a patched build if one ships. No application-side change is required while no signature-verification path reaches node-forge.
evidence:
**Advisory evidence:** `CVE-2026-85393` applies to `node-forge` at installed version `1.4.0`. The advisory is fixed in `none published yet`.

**Transitive dependency:** introduced by the direct dependency `firebase-admin@12.7.0`.

**Dependency chain:** `firebase-admin@12.7.0 > node-forge@1.4.0`

**Usage analysis:** imported by application code; affected API usage unconfirmed. Dependency edge verified: node_modules/firebase-admin/package.json lists node-forge in dependencies; firebase-admin is a direct dependency in package.json (^12.7.0) used for push notifications. Application code search (rg over src/) found zero imports of node-forge and no certificate/RSA signature-verification flow reachable from request handlers. The vulnerable symbol is not called by application code; the only consumer is firebase-admin internals whose inputs here are FCM device tokens and the Firebase service account (operator-controlled, stored at repo root). This is a prioritization signal from static analysis, not a proof of exploitability or of safety.
assumptions: Advisory data verified against the trivy-offline GHSA/Red Hat database (web search unavailable in this sandbox); installed version 1.4.0 confirmed from node_modules; no fixed version published yet at scan time. Exploitability would additionally require a low-exponent RSA key in a signature-verification flow reachable by attacker-supplied data.

dependency_metadata.reachability_evidence: Dependency edge verified: node_modules/firebase-admin/package.json lists node-forge in dependencies; firebase-admin is a direct dependency in package.json (^12.7.0) used for push notifications. Application code search (rg over src/) found zero imports of node-forge and no certificate/RSA signature-verification flow reachable from request handlers. The vulnerable symbol is not called by application code; the only consumer is firebase-admin internals whose inputs here are FCM device tokens and the Firebase service account (operator-controlled, stored at repo root).
dependency_metadata.contextual_cvss_reasoning: node-forge 1.4.0 is a direct dependency of firebase-admin (node_modules/firebase-admin/package.json dependencies list node-forge), which the app imports for FCM push notifications. I searched src/ for imports of node-forge: none — the app itself never calls node-forge APIs directly, and I found no code path where firebase-admin feeds attacker-supplied certificates or RSA material into node-forge's PKCS#1 v1.5 verification (push-token registration sends only device tokens, not certificates). The vulnerable symbol is therefore present in node_modules but has no demonstrated attacker-controlled call path in this codebase. Per the reachability rubric this is reported as imported with the trace documented and the impact scored conservatively: integrity:L only, high complexity, because exploitation requires a low-exponent RSA key in a path this app does not appear to exercise.

title: deepmerge-ts 7.1.5 stack exhaustion on recursive object graphs (CVE-2026-40345) — transitive, not imported by app code
description: deepmerge-ts 7.1.5 (transitive via @prisma/config and html-to-text) lacks visited-object tracking in deepmerge/deepmergeCustom/deepmergeInto, allowing stack exhaustion on self-referential object graphs.
impact: No attacker-reachable path identified in this codebase; documented for dependency hygiene and upgrade tracking.
remediation_steps: No urgent action; upgrade @prisma/client (which will pull a fixed deepmerge-ts tree) during the next routine dependency refresh.
evidence:
**Advisory evidence:** `CVE-2026-40345` applies to `deepmerge-ts` at installed version `7.1.5`. The advisory is fixed in `8.0.0`.

**Transitive dependency:** introduced by the direct dependency `@prisma/client@6.19.3`.

**Dependency chain:** `@prisma/client@6.19.3 > @prisma/config > deepmerge-ts@7.1.5`

**Usage analysis:** not imported by application code. rg over src/ found no import of deepmerge-ts. Dependents verified from node_modules: @prisma/config/package.json and html-to-text/package.json declare it. html-to-text is itself not imported by application code. @prisma/config's usage is internal to the Prisma toolchain operating on repo-local configuration, not request data. This is a prioritization signal from static analysis, not a proof of exploitability or of safety.
assumptions: Advisory data verified against the trivy-offline GHSA database (web search unavailable in this sandbox); installed version 7.1.5 confirmed from node_modules. Exploitability requires attacker-controlled recursive object graphs reaching deepmerge-ts, which this codebase does not appear to present.

title: uuid 10.0.0 out-of-bounds write with caller-provided buffers (CVE-2026-41907) — transitive, not imported
description: uuid 10.0.0 (transitive via firebase-admin/gaxios) does not reject out-of-range writes when v3/v5/v6 accept caller-provided output buffers (CVE-2026-41907).
impact: No attacker-reachable path in this codebase; documented for dependency hygiene and upgrade tracking.
remediation_steps: No action beyond routine upgrades; the next firebase-admin refresh will carry a fixed uuid.
evidence:
**Advisory evidence:** `CVE-2026-41907` applies to `uuid` at installed version `10.0.0`. The advisory is fixed in `11.1.1`.

**Transitive dependency:** introduced by the direct dependency `firebase-admin@12.7.0`.

**Dependency chain:** `firebase-admin@12.7.0 > uuid@10.0.0`

**Usage analysis:** not imported by application code. rg over src/ found no import of uuid (application uses crypto.randomUUID, e.g. src/routes/analysis.routes.ts share-token generation). Dependents verified from node_modules package.json edges: firebase-admin, gaxios, gcp-metadata, google-gax. None of these receive caller-provided output buffers from request handlers in this app. This is a prioritization signal from static analysis, not a proof of exploitability or of safety.
assumptions: Advisory data verified against the trivy-offline GHSA database (web search unavailable in this sandbox); installed version 10.0.0 confirmed from node_modules. The application never imports uuid, so the precondition (calling v3/v5/v6 with caller-provided buffers) is not met anywhere in this codebase.

dependency_metadata.reachability_evidence: rg over src/ found no import of uuid (application uses crypto.randomUUID, e.g. src/routes/analysis.routes.ts share-token generation). Dependents verified from node_modules package.json edges: firebase-admin, gaxios, gcp-metadata, google-gax. None of these receive caller-provided output buffers from request handlers in this app.

The vulnerability requires the application to call uuid v3/v5/v6 with an externally supplied output buffer and attacker-influenced offset — neither the app nor, to my inspection, any dependent's reachable path does this with request data.
